nih.rationale: Driven by No responses on items 5, 14, and 12: no sample size or power justification, no blinding of outcome assessors reported, and statistical adjustment covered only a limited set of confounders (age, hypertension, diabetes, admission date) while acknowledged key confounders - proning on ECMO and higher BMI in the optimal PEEP group - were not adjusted for, which the authors themselves flag. Strengths preventing a Poor rating include a clearly stated question and population (items 1, 2), near-complete inclusion of eligible patients (item 3), uniform protocol-defined exposure preceding outcomes (items 4, 6, 9), objectively defined outcomes (item 11), complete follow-up to mortality outcomes (items 7, 13), and repeated PEEP measurement (item 10). The residual confounding by temporal practice change (proning, pandemic phase) leaves more than minimal but not fatal risk of bias, consistent with a Fair rating.
